title: Your gut rebuilds itself every few days

lines.text: The inside of your gut is brand new. Again.
The lining of your digestive tract is replaced roughly every four to five days.
It has to. That lining takes a beating from acid, enzymes, and everything you eat.
So cells are constantly shed from the surface, and new ones are made underneath.
It's one of the fastest renewing tissues in your whole body.
Compare that to your skeleton, which renews only about 10% a year.
So the gut you had last week is already gone.
You are, quite literally, not the same person you were a few days ago.

sources.claim: The gut tube epithelium is completely replaced every 4–5 days in a healthy individual
Adults remodel about 10% of the skeleton per year
